Cape Cod reserves

Source: R/reserving.R
cape_cod.Rd

Bornhuetter-Ferguson reserves whose expected loss ratio is estimated from the triangle: the latest claims over the premium already earned by development (the used-up premium).

Usage

cape_cod(triangle, premium, decay = 1, ...)

Arguments

triangle

A triangle of cumulative claims, as for chain_ladder, or the result of chain_ladder(), whose development pattern is then used.

premium

The premium (or other exposure) of each origin.

decay

The weight of an origin one period away in an origin's loss ratio, from 0 to 1 (the default, the classical Cape Cod with one loss ratio).

...

Arguments passed to chain_ladder() for the development pattern, such as average and tail, when triangle is a triangle.

Value

An object of class netsimr_reserve, as for bornhuetter_ferguson, whose loss ratios are the estimated ones.

Details

The expected loss ratio is \(LR = \sum_i C_i / \sum_i P_i p_i\), with \(p_i = 1 / CDF_i\) the share developed of origin \(i\), and each origin's ultimate is \(C_i + (1 - p_i) P_i LR\). With decay below 1 (the generalised Cape Cod of Gluck), each origin has its own loss ratio, in which origin \(k\) weighs \(decay^{|i - k|}\), so that nearby origins count most; with decay 0 the method is the chain ladder.

References

Stanard, J. N. (1985). A simulation test of prediction errors of loss reserve estimation techniques. Proceedings of the Casualty Actuarial Society 72, 124-148.

Gluck, S. M. (1997). Balancing development and trend in loss reserve analysis. Proceedings of the Casualty Actuarial Society 84, 482-532.

Examples

premium <- c(50000, 52000, 54000, 56000, 58000, 60000, 62000, 64000, 66000, 68000)
cape_cod(raa_triangle, premium)
